question: I sell to customers in other EU countries. Do I have to register for VAT elsewhere, and whose VAT do I charge?

eu_b2c_threshold_eur.label: EU-wide threshold for cross-border B2C sales of goods and digital services by EU-established sellers
eu_b2c_threshold_eur.basis: Council Directive 2006/112/EC, Article 59c (inserted by Directive (EU) 2017/2455), in force since 1 July 2021. Counted across all other member states together, for the current and the previous calendar year.

ioss_consignment_limit_eur.label: Intrinsic value limit per consignment for the Import One Stop Shop (goods shipped from outside the EU to EU consumers)

oss_return_deadline.value: end of the month following each calendar quarter
oss_return_deadline.label: Union and non-Union OSS quarterly return and payment deadline
oss_return_deadline.basis: Council Directive 2006/112/EC, Article 369f (non-Union) and Article 369g/369i (Union scheme): quarterly return by the end of the month following the quarter.

uk_vat_registration_threshold_gbp.label: UK VAT registration threshold for UK-established businesses (non-UK sellers of B2C digital services to UK consumers must register from the first sale)
uk_vat_registration_threshold_gbp.basis: Value Added Tax Act 1994 Schedule 1 as amended; threshold GBP 90,000 from 1 April 2024.

limits: An estimate from the rules above, not advice on your situation. Member states apply the directive through national law and procedure.

Excluded: excise goods, new means of transport, margin-scheme goods, services connected to land, admission to events, passenger transport, restaurant and catering, and sellers established in more than one member state.
Figures are checked against the official pages on the as_of date. Confirm them there before you register or file.
